input: For patient 170 in random forest trained at 1:3, first separate biomarkers that push the prediction toward versus away from depression. Among the toward-depression group, keep the strongest 2; then use each one's overall SHAP tendency to derive a model-based direction for reducing its contribution.
output:
<PLAN>
BINDINGS = {"patient":170,"model":"random forest","ratio":"1:3","k":2}
P1 = RETRIEVE(relation="local_shap", patient=$patient, model=$model, ratio=$ratio, feature=ALL, fields=["value","direction"])
P2 = GROUP(input=P1, key="direction", groups=["positive","negative"])
P3 = RANK(input=P2.positive, key="local_shap", order="descending", top_k=$k)
P4 = RETRIEVE(relation="global_shap_tendency", model=$model, ratio=$ratio, features=P3.features)
P5 = APPLY_RULE(inputs=[P3,P4], rule="if increasing feature lowers SHAP -> increase; if increasing feature raises SHAP -> decrease")
</PLAN>
<DECOMPOSITION>
Step 1: Retrieve local SHAP values and separate positive from negative contributors.
Sub-question: For patient 170 in random forest trained at 1:3, which biomarkers have positive local SHAP values and which have negative local SHAP values?  # Type: searching
Step 2: Select the 2 strongest biomarkers from the positive-contribution group.
Sub-question: Among the positive local-SHAP biomarkers for patient 170, which 2 have the largest local SHAP values?  # Type: aggregation
Step 3: Retrieve the global SHAP tendency for the selected biomarkers.
Sub-question: For those 2 selected biomarkers in random forest at 1:3, as each biomarker increases, does its global SHAP tendency increase or decrease the depression prediction?  # Type: searching
Step 4: Convert the global tendencies into model-based directions.
Sub-question: For each selected positive contributor, map decreasing global SHAP tendency to INCREASE and increasing global SHAP tendency to DECREASE.  # Type: aggregation
</DECOMPOSITION>

P1 = RETRIEVE(relation="local_shap", patient=$patient, models=$models, ratio=$ratio, feature=$feature, fields=["value","direction"])

input: Using naive bayes at 1:2 for patient 215, focus on the 2 strongest biomarkers from the positive local-SHAP group. For each, determine whether increasing or decreasing it would be associated with lower SHAP according to its global tendency.
output:
<PLAN>
BINDINGS = {"patient":215,"model":"naive bayes","ratio":"1:2","k":2}
P1 = RETRIEVE(relation="local_shap", patient=$patient, model=$model, ratio=$ratio, feature=ALL, fields=["value","direction"])
P2 = GROUP(input=P1, key="direction", groups=["positive","negative"])
P3 = RANK(input=P2.positive, key="local_shap", order="descending", top_k=$k)
P4 = RETRIEVE(relation="global_shap_tendency", model=$model, ratio=$ratio, features=P3.features)
P5 = APPLY_RULE(inputs=[P3,P4], rule="if increasing feature lowers SHAP -> increase; if increasing feature raises SHAP -> decrease")
</PLAN>
<DECOMPOSITION>
Step 1: Retrieve local SHAP values and separate positive from negative contributors.
Sub-question: For patient 215 in naive bayes trained at 1:2, which biomarkers have positive local SHAP values and which have negative local SHAP values?  # Type: searching
Step 2: Select the 2 strongest biomarkers from the positive-contribution group.
Sub-question: Among the positive local-SHAP biomarkers for patient 215, which 2 have the largest local SHAP values?  # Type: aggregation
Step 3: Retrieve the global SHAP tendency for the selected biomarkers.
Sub-question: For those 2 selected biomarkers in naive bayes at 1:2, as each biomarker increases, does its global SHAP tendency increase or decrease the depression prediction?  # Type: searching
Step 4: Convert the global tendencies into model-based directions.
Sub-question: For each selected positive contributor, map decreasing global SHAP tendency to INCREASE and increasing global SHAP tendency to DECREASE.  # Type: aggregation
</DECOMPOSITION>
